entries.title: Internal asset: we1149srv
entries.note: Public web server for the company website. Windows Server with IIS, PHP and MySQL; runs the website's content management system. Owner: web team. Should accept inbound web traffic only; it has no business browsing out to the internet.

entries.title: Internal asset: 192.168.250.70
entries.note: See 192.168.250.70. Public web server for the company website.

entries.title: Shared dynamic-DNS domain
entries.note: A free dynamic-DNS service: anyone can register a subdomain and point it at any IP address in minutes, without verification. The parent domain tells you nothing about who owns a subdomain. Subdomains of free dynamic-DNS services turn up often in opportunistic attacks because they're free, quick and disposable.

entries.title: Script, not a browser
entries.note: The default User-Agent of Python 2.7's urllib library. Browsers never send it. Seeing it against a login page means someone is automating requests.

entries.title: eXtplorer (Joomla extension)
entries.note: A web-based file manager that can be installed into Joomla. A legitimate admin tool, but anyone who gets into the admin panel can use it to upload files to the web server.

entries.title: Built-in IIS account
entries.note: NT AUTHORITY\IUSR is the built-in account IIS uses for anonymous web requests. It should be able to read the website's files and nothing more. A program the web server launches runs with its rights.

entries.title: PHP interpreter
entries.note: Runs the PHP pages of the website for IIS. Normally it doesn't start other programs. php-cgi.exe launching cmd.exe is a classic web-shell pattern.
